title: identity/status and identity/link
description: Who the user is on their OWN mesh, and the gesture that links this machine to it. Meltemi has no accounts and issues no identity: it reads the official client of the mesh the user already runs, the way the daemon reads `git`, and it never touches that client's tokens. `identity/status` answers `available: false` with a reason when there is no `[identity]` table, no client where it was named, or a client that is present and not signed in — an answer, not a failure, because a user who never wanted identity is not in a broken state. `identity/link` composes the gesture and hands it back as text; the daemon never runs it, because a daemon that executed a login would be a daemon holding someone's session.

unavailableReason.description: not_configured: no [identity] table in the user's configuration; client_missing: the mesh client was not found where the configuration named it; not_linked: the client is there and this machine has not signed in. Three reasons because each asks for a different remedy.

presence.description: Whether the machine is reachable on the mesh right now. Presence, not control: Meltemi offers nothing that acts on another machine because it knows one is online.

machine.description: One machine of the user's mesh, as that mesh's own client reports it.

system.description: The operating system the mesh reports, when it reports one.

lastSeen.description: When the mesh last saw it (RFC 3339, UTC), when it says.

thisMachine.description: Whether this is the machine the daemon runs on.

statusParams.description: Params of `identity/status`: none. Identity belongs to the person and the machine, not to a project, so no project root is taken.

remedy.description: What to do about that reason, in English like every remedy of the daemon.

user.description: Who the user is on their mesh, as the mesh names them. Never a Meltemi account, because there are none.

provider.description: Which mesh answered: the value of `[identity] mesh`.

this.description: This machine's name on the mesh.

machines.description: The user's machines. Empty when identity is unavailable, and empty is not an error: a mesh of one machine is a mesh.

hostname.description: The name to ask the mesh for, when the user wants one of their choosing.

linkResult.description: The gesture, as text, in both shells. Handed back and never run.

command.description: The gesture as one line, for reading and copying.

opensBrowser.description: Whether running it is expected to open a browser, so a surface can say so before the user is surprised by one.

loginServer.description: The login server the gesture names, when the configuration set one.
